qt: to the Commission Aurélia Beigneux (ID) Subject:

Milk glass presents particular difficulties because of its composition and appearance, making recycling complicated and posing waste management challenges. Because of its milky appearance and translucency, it can be difficult to sort effectively at recycling centres, diminishing the quality of the recycled glass and its ability to be reused in new products. Because of the EU’s environmental objectives, craftspeople are now being urged to make use of it on a very large scale. However, it is extremely important that recycling processes in Europe should be as efficient and clean as possible. Accordingly: 1.
How does the Commission intend to encourage and facilitate the recycling of milk glass?
What measures does the Commission plan to take to encourage research and development regarding more advanced sorting techniques capable of distinguishing milk glass from other types of glass?

(22 April 2024) The proposed EU Regulation on Packaging and Packaging Waste (1), on which the co-legislators reached preliminary agreement on 4 March 2024, aims to foster sustainability in the packaging sector by implementing measures that encourage eco-friendly packaging practices and materials. Packaging made of milk glass is not specifically addressed in the proposed regulation because it accounts for a very small part of the total volume of glass packaging waste. However, measures envisaged in the regulation, in particular the rules to ensure that all packaging is recyclable and recycled at scale will ensure that packaging formats that cannot be recycled will be phased out by 2030. These measures will drive advancement in the sorting and recycling of packaging waste. Ensuring the effective collection, sorting and recycling of packaging is primarily subject to the extended producer responsibility (EPR) of economic operators placing packaging on the market. The new packaging regulation will strengthen the incentives to improve packaging circularity, both through the recyclability requirements referred to above and through the modulation of EPR fees based on their recyclability. More generally, research and innovation projects in the environmental area can be funded through the Horizon Programm e (2) or the EU programme for the environment and climate action (3) in accordance with their rules.
